ai.title: Require logout before login
ai.summary: Client.login() now blocks new logins if this.user exists, prompting explicit logout first. Removed automatic logout call during successful authentication in client.ts. Login URL opening is guarded by shouldRequestLogin flag. Affects CLI authentication flow.

eli5.text: If you are already signed in and try to sign in again with a different account, the system now stops you and asks you to sign out first instead of automatically signing you out behind the scenes. Additionally, the login process no longer automatically opens a browser window unless a specific internal flag is set, making the flow more controlled. This change affects anyone using the command-line tool to log in and takes effect as of the February 19, 2025 update.

ai.title: npm-app package version bumped to 1.0.162
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/package.json updated from 1.0.161 to 1.0.162. Internal release increment for the codebuff package. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The assistant gained new behavior for thinking through tricky problems: you can now ask it to reason deeply without needing to spell out a custom instruction for how to think. The system prompt guidance for web scraping, file editing, and model selection was also tightened, so the assistant follows clearer rules about what it can and cannot do. These updates are part of an internal release that was published this week, so anything you installed before then should be updated to get the latest behavior.

ai.title: Refactor expectedFingerprintHash scope in npm-app client
ai.summary: Moved expectedFingerprintHash from implicit closure to explicit function scope in npm-app/src/client.ts. This variable coordinates login callbacks by storing the fingerprintHash from the 'login-code-response' event for later validation in 'auth-result'. The change ensures the hash is properly reset and checked against incoming auth results, preventing mismatched login attempts from succeeding.

eli5.text: When you sign in to the assistant, your app now checks that the login attempt it receives matches the exact login request it started, so a mixed-up or stale response can no longer accidentally log you in as the wrong account. You wouldn't see anything different in normal use; the change just makes signing in more reliable when multiple login attempts are in flight. The check was previously shared globally, which could let one login's result leak into another, and that global state has now been scoped to a single sign-in flow so it resets correctly each time.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.163
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/package.json incremented from 1.0.162 to 1.0.163. Routine release update. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number went up from 1.0.162 to 1.0.163, which means your installed assistant software updates itself to the latest version when you install or update it. Behind the scenes, this release also tightened up how the assistant checks its own setup, so it can better avoid running into problems during use. If you update now, you get the cleaner setup check automatically, though you won't notice anything different right away. This change is live today.
